findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Finite.lean:352 `Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton M] : Module.finrank R M = 0`; mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Basic.lean:54 `Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff : Nontrivial (R ⧸ I) ↔ I ≠ ⊤`. Note `Algebra.finrank_eq_one_iff_bijective_algebraMap` (FreeAndStrongRankCondition.lean:298) itself needs no `Nontrivial` hypothesis.
findings.fix: Drop `hI` from the statement and derive it in the proof: `Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff.mp` applied to the nontriviality that follows from `Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton` contradicting `hdeg` (or from injectivity of `algebraMap F (F[W] ⧸ I)` given by `hbij`). Then drop the `v.isPrime.ne_top` argument at line 224.
findings.issue: `exists_equation_and_eq_XYIdeal` takes `hI : I ≠ ⊤` alongside `hdeg : Module.finrank F (F[W] ⧸ I) = 1`, but `hdeg` already implies it: `I = ⊤` makes the quotient subsingleton, so its finrank is `0`. The redundant hypothesis is in the public surface and forces work on every caller — `exists_pointPlace_eq` (line 224) has to supply `v.isPrime.ne_top`.

findings.evidence: TauCeti/.../XYIdealMaximal.lean:94-101 states the general form and derives the point case with `_of_equation`; mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Point.lean:259 `quotientXYIdealEquiv {x : R} {y : R[X]} (h : (W'.polynomial.eval y).eval x = 0)`.
findings.fix: State `finrank_quotient_XYIdeal {y : F[X]} (h : (W.polynomial.eval y).eval x = 0)` and add the point case as `finrank_quotient_XYIdeal_of_equation`, matching `XYIdeal_isMaximal` / `XYIdeal_isMaximal_of_equation` in the sibling file.
findings.issue: `finrank_quotient_XYIdeal` is stated only for the constant `C y`, though `quotientXYIdealEquiv` and its one-line proof are valid for arbitrary `y : F[X]` under `(W.polynomial.eval y).eval x = 0`. A consumer holding a general `XYIdeal W x y` (the form `XYIdeal_isMaximal`, `XYIdeal_eq_iff_of_ne_top`, and Mathlib's `XYIdeal_eq₁`/`XYIdeal_eq₂`/`XYIdeal_add_eq` all produce) gets nothing, and the unsuffixed name promises the general lemma.

findings.evidence: Lines 231-245: `Equiv.ofBijective` plus `coe_equationEquivPointPlace` only; no `_symm_apply` lemma exists in the file (`grep -n symm TauCeti/.../Point/Place.lean` returns nothing).
findings.fix: Add the elimination lemma, e.g. `@[simp] theorem pointPlace_symm_apply (v : {v // Module.finrank F (W.CoordinateRing ⧸ v.asIdeal) = 1}) : pointPlace ((equationEquivPointPlace W).symm v).2 = (v : HeightOneSpectrum W.CoordinateRing)`, provable by `simp [← coe_equationEquivPointPlace]`.
findings.issue: `equationEquivPointPlace` is built by `Equiv.ofBijective`, so its inverse is opaque, and only the forward map is characterised (`coe_equationEquivPointPlace`). Reading the dictionary backwards — the direction this PR exists to add — has no lemma; `exists_pointPlace_eq` gives only non-canonical existence.

summary: The classification carries a redundant properness hypothesis that every consumer must discharge, the new finrank lemma is stated more narrowly than the sibling `XYIdeal` API it parallels, and the dictionary equivalence characterises only its forward direction.
